chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from one who narrated it from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man committed fornication with a woman; is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said: What a forbidden thing has ever made a permissible thing permissible. The ruling in these two narrations and what follows their pattern, which includes the wording of marriage in the future or present, is that if the fornication was with the woman without sexual intercourse and penetration, then as for with intercourse and penetration, it is not permissible, according to what we have previously mentioned, which indicates this distinction.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of the woman he had sex with?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibition of marrying the daughter of a man who fornicated with her mother is not absolute but contingent on the nature of the act; specifically, if the fornication involved only partial intimacy without full penetration (idha'), the marriage remains permissible. This ruling distinguishes between minor and major forms of illicit sexual relations, reflecting the juristic principle that the severity of the act determines the extent of the marital impediment (mahram relationship).
